exposure: Timing of GDM screening (early, standard, late)
cohort: Adult pregnant women with a high risk of GDM (n=803) from a hospital in Northeast Mexico.
finding: The study found a similar proportion of GDM diagnoses across early, standard, and late screening times, with no additional benefits on neonatal outcomes from early or late screening; however, women with GDM had significantly earlier gestational age at birth and higher rates of caesarean section.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was significantly more frequent in women diagnosed with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus compared with women without GDM.
cross-section timing: Screening for GDM was performed at early, standard (24-28 weeks), or late gestational ages, with outcomes assessed at the end of pregnancy and birth.
gest_age: Mean gestational age at the end of pregnancy was 37.6+4.4 weeks across the cohort, with earlier gestational age at birth being an outcome for women with GDM.
